result.sentence: The revenue requirement is $783,333,333. Each point of return on equity is worth $13,333,333 a year, about $0.89 a month per home.

work.method: Revenue requirement = O&M + depreciation + taxes other than income + income tax + rate base × weighted cost of capital, where the weighted cost of capital is equity share × return on equity + debt share × cost of debt, and income tax on the equity return is that return × t ÷ (1 − t).
steps: Weighted cost of capital: 50% equity × 10% + 50% debt × 5% = 7.5%.
Income tax on the equity return: $100,000,000 × 25% ÷ (1 − 25%) = $33,333,333.
Revenue requirement: O&M $400,000,000 + depreciation $150,000,000 + other taxes $50,000,000 + income tax $33,333,333 + return $150,000,000 = $783,333,333.
One point less return on equity (10% to 9%) lowers it by $13,333,333: $10,000,000 of return and $3,333,333 of income tax.
Per home: $13,333,333 × 40% residential share ÷ 500,000 residential customers ÷ 12 = $0.89 a month. This is an approximation: rates are not set by revenue share alone.
assumptions: Income tax is grossed up on the equity return only, at one combined rate; deferred taxes and tax credits are left out.
The per-home figure spreads a change in proportion to the residential share of revenue; a rate case's cost allocation can differ.

citations.source: Regulatory Assistance Project, Electricity Regulation in the US: A Guide
citations.locator: Chapter 9, the revenue requirement and its components

result.validationMeaning: Our own worked examples and consistency tests pass, but no independent check has been run yet.
